uncited: The FDK Backprojection Transpose computes the adjoint of the forward FDK projection operator, scattering voxel values from a 3D volume back to 2D projection panels.
It solves the problem of computing the gradient of the data fidelity term with respect to the projection data in differentiable tomographic reconstruction.

Unlike the forward pass which projects volume to projections, this method accumulates projection values into a buffer using atomic operations, serving as the transpose of the linear system matrix $A$ in the equation $Ax=b$.
- `matrices`: 4D tensor of shape `[batch, views, 12]` containing camera extrinsics (source and detector positions/orientations).
- Detach and convert `matrices` to contiguous float32.
- Create `out` tensor of shape `[batch, 1, views, rows, columns]` filled with zeros.
- Extract dimensions: `batch`, `depth`, `height`, `width` from `volume.shape`; `views`, `rows`, `columns` from `projection_shape`.
- Launch CUDA kernel `fdk_backproject_transpose_c1` with grid size `(depth, height, width)` and block size `_VOLUME_BLOCK`.
- Pass arguments: `volume[item, 0]`, `matrices`, `out[item, 0]`, `width`, `height`, `depth`, `views`, `rows`, `columns`.
- Each thread handles a block of voxels along the z-axis: `z0 = blockIdx.z * TT_FDK_DEPTH`.
- Thread indices `(x, y)` map to volume coordinates.
- Load `TT_FDK_DEPTH` voxel values from `volume` at `(x, y, z0...z0+3)`.
- If all loaded values are zero, skip the view loop.
- Compute `ViewColumn` parameters from `matrices`.
- Compute ray path through the volume for this voxel.
- Perform `atomicAdd(out[s.index[q]], s.weight[q] * value[j])`.
- **Atomic Contention**: Multiple threads may write to the same projection pixel simultaneously.
Note that `float32` addition is not associative, so the order of accumulation matters for numerical consistency with the forward pass.
- **Time Complexity**: $O(B \cdot V \cdot D \cdot H \cdot W)$, where $B$ is batch size, $V$ is views, $D,H,W$ are volume dimensions.
- **Memory Complexity**: $O(B \cdot V \cdot R \cdot C)$ for the output buffer.
- **Performance**: The kernel is optimized for CUDA, using shared memory for view parameters and atomic operations for accumulation.
Performance is limited by atomic contention on high-resolution projections or large batch sizes.
Integrates seamlessly with PyTorch via custom CUDA kernels.
Numerical precision issues may arise due to non-associative floating-point addition in `atomicAdd`.
The FDK Backprojection Transpose is part of the `torchtomo` library, which provides differentiable tomographic reconstruction tools.
It implements the adjoint of the FDK (Feldkamp-Davis-Kress) projection operator, enabling gradient-based optimization in tomographic imaging.
The method was developed to support end-to-end differentiable pipelines in medical imaging and materials science.
